question: Does the positive N_eff coefficient persist after conditioning on one- and two-year demographic momentum, or is N_eff merely a proxy for recent decline inertia?

models.original: next_growth ~ island + z(log1p current abundance) + z(year) + z(log1p N_eff)

fixed_checks.coefficient: standardized N_eff coefficient remains positive and close in magnitude to the original +0.1167989675
fixed_checks.prediction: report leave-one-end-year-out C0-C1 MSE gain without restoring a predictive claim
fixed_checks.structured_null: reuse the already-frozen full-series island-wise circular-shift family; no new permutation family is introduced
fixed_checks.joint_null: reuse the exact 26 x 16 persistent-islands/Litchfield shift family preserving cross-island N_eff covariance among persistent islands

sample_rule.lag1_lag2: complete cases for growth[t-1] and growth[t-2]

supported_if: lag1 and lag1+lag2 N_eff coefficients remain positive
both coefficients remain unusual under the reused structured-null family
not_supported: a claim that demographic momentum has no ecological role

terminal_rule: This closes the demographic-momentum confounding check. Do not add lag3+, alternative smoothing windows, autoregressive orders, or new N_eff null families to rescue or enlarge the claim.
